applicant_utility.summary: FIRST@IITH funds a four-year PhD at IIT Hyderabad for foreign nationals holding a master's degree in engineering or technology with a CGPA of at least 8.5/10, paying Rs 60,000 per month plus Rs 1,00,000 per year in contingency support. The current January 2027 round is email-only: the completed form, testimonials and at least one reference letter must reach ia.ir@iith.ac.in with the exact subject line 'Application for FIRST@IITH fellowship - January-2027' by 17:00 IST on 31 October 2026. OCI and NRI candidates are excluded, and both the bachelor's and master's degrees must come from foreign universities, so an India-taught degree at either level disqualifies you. The published package supports living costs and research contingency; the pages do not state a tuition waiver, so plan around IITH's fee, hostel, mess and insurance charges.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Foreign-national master's graduates in engineering or technology from overseas universities with strong grades and early research output (publications or patents) who want a funded four-year PhD in India.

Send the email well before 17:00 IST on 31 October 2026 using the exact intake-specific subject line
common_rejection_risks: OCI or NRI status, or a bachelor's or master's degree earned at an Indian university
CGPA below 8.5/10 or an equivalence the committee cannot verify

Exceeding the 2500-character limits for the research outline or statement of purpose
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The official package is the Rs 60,000 monthly fellowship plus Rs 1,00,000 annual contingency; the FIRST@IITH pages do not publish a tuition waiver and direct fee queries to IITH's fee-structure page, so tuition (if charged), hostel, mess and medical insurance per IITH norms remain the fellow's own responsibility.

GRE/IELTS/TOEFL year and score are requested but 'NA' is accepted if not available, so missing test scores do not block the application

verification.notes: Fellowship amount (Rs 1,35,000 per month consolidated including HRA), research grant (Rs 7.00 lakh per annum), overheads (Rs 60,000 per annum), five-year non-extendable duration, eligibility rules, nomination procedure and required documents were all confirmed on ANRF's official Ramanujan Fellowship page and its FAQ; the page publishes no English language requirement and no fixed deadline.

applicant_utility.summary: The ANRF Ramanujan Fellowship funds Indian and Indian-origin scientists working abroad to take up a five-year, non-extendable research position in India, paying Rs 1,35,000 per month consolidated (including HRA), Rs 7 lakh per year in research grant and Rs 60,000 per year in overheads to the host institute. There is no deadline: you register on the ANRF portal, complete the nomination form and send it to the head of your chosen host institution, who verifies and submits it, with selections made periodically. The two real gatekeepers are securing a willing host outside your PhD-granting institute and staying under 40 while working abroad with no Indian position. The fellowship is taxable, cannot be combined with any institutional salary, and must be joined within six months of the selection intimation letter.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Indian-origin researchers under 40, currently employed abroad with a strong publication and recognition record, who want an independent five-year research career at an Indian institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up a host institution that will provide administrative and R&D basic infrastructural support, and that is not the institute where you did your PhD
Confirm you hold no permanent, tenure-track or contractual position anywhere in India and are working abroad on the nomination date
Prepare the nomination letter, plagiarism undertaking and other technical document using ANRF's prescribed templates, on letterhead, signed and stamped
Condense the proposed research area and proposal outline into a single PDF of no more than 5 pages
Complete every mandatory ANRF portal profile field (photo, institution, address) before starting the form, and be ready to join within six months of selection
common_rejection_risks: Nomination from your PhD supervisor or from the same institute where you pursued your PhD - such nominations are not considered
Holding or accepting any permanent, tenure-track or contractual Indian position before or during the fellowship
Being 40 years or older at the time of nomination
A proposal that merely continues the doctorate work instead of opening a new research area and laboratory
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The Rs 1,35,000 consolidated stipend is the personal income; the research grant and overheads are spent through the host institute, so relocation, housing and personal costs beyond the stipend are the fellow's own, and the stipend is taxable as per IT rules.
document_audit: The nomination letter must be on the host institution's letterhead, duly signed and stamped, using ANRF's template
The proposal must be a single PDF of five pages maximum - split or oversized files break the submission
Plagiarism undertaking and Other Technical Document must follow the prescribed RJF formats, not free-form letters
Second-year funding requires a year-wise Statement of Expenditure, Utilization Certificate and progress report, so keep financial records from day one
alerts: Taking any permanent, tenure-track or contractual position in India forces you to relinquish the fellowship in total, including the research grant and overheads
The fellowship cannot be combined with salary from the host institute, and only one international travel per year is supported
Host-institute transfer is possible only while you hold no permanent, tenure-track or contractual position, and requires NOCs from both institutions
Selection timing is unpredictable because the empowered Selection Committee meets periodically with no published calendar
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Nominee completes the Ramanujan Fellowship nomination form on the ANRF portal and clicks 'Send to Nominator'; the host institution head reviews the packet, verifies it and submits the nomination to ANRF, after which both parties receive submission confirmation.
